answer: In an agent marketplace selling goods from velvet to violet dye, even a seller on a remote knoll must lock 100 tokens for 30 days per trading identity. Each identity's outstanding orders are capped at its bond, and proven non-delivery forfeits collateral to buyers. An attacker running 1,000 fake sellers must immobilize 100,000 tokens; splitting into more identities creates no extra unsecured selling capacity and puts real capital at risk.
